sections.title: X2 hardware design spec
sections.text: Nimbus X2 Smart Thermostat - Hardware Design Specification Document HW-X2-001, Revision C, 12 September 2026. Confidential - internal use only.

sections.title: 1 Overview
sections.text: The Nimbus X2 is the second-generation smart thermostat from Nimbus Home. It replaces the X1 platform with a faster microcontroller, a larger color display, on-board CO2 sensing and a Wi-Fi 6 / Bluetooth LE 5.3 radio. The product targets North American low-voltage (24 VAC) residential HVAC systems, including conventional furnaces, heat pumps with auxiliary heat and two-stage cooling. Key design goals for X2 were a 30% reduction in bill-of-materials cost relative to X1, support for installations without a common (C) wire through power stealing, and a standby consumption below 0.5 W to meet ENERGY STAR Smart Thermostat v1.1 requirements.
sections.summary: Introduces the Nimbus X2 smart thermostat hardware, its target market and the scope and revision history of this specification.

sections.title: 1.1 Scope
sections.text: This document covers the main board (PCB-X2-MB), the relay board (PCB-X2-RB) and the interface between them. Firmware behavior is specified in FW-X2-004 and enclosure tooling in ME-X2-002. All voltages are nominal unless stated otherwise.
sections.summary: Defines what this specification covers (electrical, mechanical interfaces, sensors) and what is covered elsewhere (firmware, enclosure tooling).

sections.title: 1.2 Revision History
sections.text: Rev Date Author Changes A 2026-03-04 L. Ortega Initial release for EVT1 B 2026-06-19 M. Chen Added CO2 sensor, updated power budget C 2026-09-12 M. Chen Relay board rework, pinout corrections, compliance section
sections.summary: Lists the three document revisions from March to September 2026 and what changed in each.

sections.title: 2 System Architecture
sections.text: The architecture is centered on a single STM32U585 microcontroller that handles the user interface, control loop and sensor fusion. A separate ESP32-C6 module provides Wi-Fi and BLE connectivity and communicates with the MCU over SPI. The block diagram below shows the main functional blocks and the buses that connect them. Figure 1: System block diagram showing MCU, radio, sensors, display, relay board and power interfaces The relay board is isolated from the main board by optocouplers so that a fault on the HVAC side cannot damage the MCU. All high-current traces are routed on the relay board only.
sections.summary: Describes the X2 architecture built around an STM32U585 MCU connected to the radio, sensors, display, relay board and power supply.

sections.title: 2.1 Main Controller
sections.text: The STM32U585 was selected for its TrustZone security, low-power modes and integrated graphics accelerator. It runs at 160 MHz with 2 MB of flash and 786 KB of SRAM. An external 16 MB QSPI flash stores UI assets and the secondary firmware slot for over-the-air updates. Core: Arm Cortex-M33 with TrustZone and FPU Clock: 160 MHz from a 16 MHz crystal plus 32.768 kHz RTC crystal Secure boot with keys stored in the OTP area Watchdog timeout: 4 seconds in normal operation
sections.summary: Details the STM32U585 MCU choice, clock, memory and its responsibilities.

sections.title: 2.2 Wireless Connectivity
sections.text: Wireless connectivity uses a pre-certified ESP32-C6-MINI module with an on-board PCB antenna. The antenna keep-out area must be at least 15 mm from the relay board and any metal backplate. BLE is used during setup for commissioning from the Nimbus mobile app; Wi-Fi is used for cloud connectivity and firmware updates.
sections.summary: Covers the ESP32-C6 Wi-Fi 6 / BLE 5.3 module, antenna placement and RF certification approach.

sections.title: 3 Power Subsystem
sections.text: The thermostat is powered from the 24 VAC R and C terminals through a full-bridge rectifier and a synchronous buck converter. When no C wire is present, the power-stealing circuit draws current through the W or Y call circuit while the relay is open, charging a 1 F supercapacitor that buffers the peak load during Wi-Fi transmission. Rail Voltage Max current Source Loads VIN 24 VAC (18-30 VAC) 250 mA HVAC transformer Rectifier input V5 5.0 V 400 mA Buck converter Relay coils, 3.3 V LDO V3P3 3.3 V 300 mA LDO MCU, radio, sensors, display logic VBL 12 V 40 mA Boost converter Display backlight Figure 2: Measured 3.3 V current draw in each operating mode Peak current occurs when a relay is switching while Wi-Fi is transmitting. Firmware staggers these events by at least 50 ms so that power-stealing installations do not brown out.
sections.summary: Explains how X2 is powered from 24 VAC, including power stealing for installations without a C wire, rail specifications and measured current draw.

sections.title: 4 Sensors
sections.text: Sensor Part Interface Accuracy Sample rate Temperature / humidity Sensirion SHT45 I2C (0x44) +/-0.1 °C, +/-1.0% RH 1 Hz CO2 Sensirion SCD41 I2C (0x62) +/-(40 ppm + 5%) 1 per 30 s Ambient light Vishay VEML7700 I2C (0x10) +/-10% 2 Hz Occupancy Panasonic EKMC1603111 GPIO 5 m range Event driven
sections.summary: Lists the temperature, humidity, CO2 and ambient light sensors used and their accuracy, then describes the factory calibration procedure.

sections.title: 4.1 Calibration
sections.text: Each unit is calibrated in a thermal chamber at 18 °C and 28 °C. The resulting offset and gain are written to the MCU option bytes. Because the display and MCU warm the enclosure by up to 1.8 °C, firmware applies a self-heating compensation model that uses backlight level and CPU load as inputs. After compensation, reported temperature must be within +/-0.3 °C of the chamber reference.
sections.summary: Describes the two-point factory temperature calibration and how self-heating from the display and MCU is compensated.

sections.title: 5 Interfaces and Pinout
sections.text: The main board connects to the relay board through a 10-pin 1.27 mm pitch board-to-board connector (J4). Revision C swapped pins 7 and 8 to simplify routing. Pin Signal Direction Description 1 V5 Out 5 V supply to relay board 2 GND - Ground 3 RLY_W Out Heat relay drive 4 RLY_Y1 Out Cool stage 1 relay drive 5 RLY_Y2 Out Cool stage 2 relay drive 6 RLY_G Out Fan relay drive 7 RLY_OB Out Heat pump reversing valve 8 C_DET In C-wire present detect 9 PS_EN Out Power-stealing enable 10 GND - Ground
sections.summary: Gives the pin assignments for the 10-pin main-to-relay-board connector.

sections.title: 6 Environmental and Compliance
sections.text: Operating temperature: 0 to 45 °C; storage -20 to 60 °C Humidity: 5 to 90% RH non-condensing FCC Part 15 Subpart B and C; ISED RSS-247 UL 60730-1 and UL 60730-2-9 (automatic electrical controls) ENERGY STAR Smart Thermostat v1.1 RoHS 3 and REACH compliant
sections.summary: Summarizes operating conditions and the regulatory certifications X2 must pass before launch.

sections.title: X2 installation and user guide
sections.text: Nimbus X2 Installation and User Guide For firmware 3.2 and later. Read all instructions before installing.

sections.title: 1 Safety Information
sections.text: The Nimbus X2 is designed for 24 V low-voltage heating and cooling systems only. Improper installation can damage your equipment or cause injury. If you are not comfortable working with household wiring, contact a licensed HVAC professional. Figure 1: Warning label printed on the back of the X2 backplate Do not connect to 120 V or 240 V line-voltage heating systems (for example baseboard heaters). Do not install in bathrooms or other locations where the unit may get wet. Keep the thermostat away from direct sunlight, drafts and heat sources such as lamps.
sections.summary: Gives the key electrical safety warnings, including switching off power at the breaker and not using X2 with line-voltage systems.

sections.title: 2 What's in the Box
sections.text: Nimbus X2 thermostat display unit Backplate with built-in level Trim plate (covers old thermostat marks) 4 screws and 4 wall anchors Wire labels sticker sheet Power adapter kit (PAK-2) for systems without a C wire Quick start card
sections.summary: Lists the package contents: thermostat, backplate, trim plate, screws, labels and the optional C-wire adapter.

sections.title: 3 Installation
sections.text: Installation typically takes about 30 minutes. You will need a Phillips screwdriver, a drill with a 3/16-inch bit for the anchors, and your smartphone with the Nimbus app installed.
sections.summary: Walks through wiring and mounting the thermostat, typically taking about 30 minutes.

sections.title: 3.1 Wiring
sections.text: Before removing your old thermostat, take a photo of its wiring and use the included stickers to label each wire by the terminal it was connected to. Wire color is not always a reliable indicator; always label by terminal letter. Figure 2: Terminal wiring for a conventional heat/cool system with fan Terminal Typical color Function Required? R / Rh / Rc Red 24 VAC power from transformer Yes C Blue or black Common (return path for 24 VAC) Recommended W / W1 White Heat stage 1 If you have heating Y / Y1 Yellow Cooling stage 1 (or compressor for heat pumps) If you have cooling G Green Fan Recommended O/B Orange or dark blue Heat pump reversing valve Heat pumps only
sections.summary: Explains how to label and connect the R, C, W, Y and G wires, with a wiring diagram and a table of standard wire colors.

sections.title: 3.2 Mounting
sections.text: 1. Turn off power to your HVAC system at the circuit breaker. 2. Remove the old thermostat and label the wires. 3. Hold the X2 backplate against the wall, level it using the built-in bubble level and mark the screw holes. 4. Drill holes, insert the anchors and screw the backplate to the wall. 5. Insert each labeled wire into the matching terminal until the button pops up. 6. Snap the display onto the backplate and turn the power back on.
sections.summary: Gives the six mounting steps from turning off power to attaching the display.

sections.title: 4 Using Your Thermostat
sections.text: After power-up, X2 guides you through setup on screen and in the Nimbus app. The home screen shows the current indoor temperature in large digits, the target temperature and what the system is doing right now. Figure 3: X2 home screen while heating Turn the outer ring to change the target temperature and press the display to open the menu. The three buttons at the bottom of the screen open the mode, fan and schedule settings.
sections.summary: Describes the home screen, the available operating modes and how to set schedules.

sections.title: 4.1 Modes
sections.text: Mode What it does Best for Heat Heats to the set temperature Winter Cool Cools to the set temperature Summer Auto Keeps temperature between a low and high set point Spring and fall Eco Uses wider set points when nobody is home Saving energy Off Heating and cooling are off; fan can still run Open-window days
sections.summary: Explains the Heat, Cool, Auto, Eco and Off modes and when to use each.

sections.title: 4.2 Schedules
sections.text: You can create up to 8 schedule points per day in the Nimbus app. With Adaptive Recovery turned on, X2 learns how long your home takes to heat or cool and starts early so that the target temperature is reached at the scheduled time, not after it.
sections.summary: Describes creating weekly schedules and how Adaptive Recovery pre-heats or pre-cools before a scheduled change.

sections.title: 5 Troubleshooting
sections.text: If X2 detects a problem it shows an error code on screen and sends a notification to the Nimbus app. Heating and cooling may pause until the problem is resolved. Figure 4: Example error screen for code E4 Code Meaning What to do E1 No power on R wire Check the breaker and the R wire connection E2 Power stealing unstable Install the PAK-2 adapter or connect a C wire E3 Wi-Fi authentication failed Re-enter the Wi-Fi password in the app E4 Temperature sensor not responding Hold MENU for 10 s to restart; contact support if it returns E5 Relay stuck Turn off power at breaker and contact support E6 Firmware image invalid Device will roll back automatically; retry update later
sections.summary: Shows an example error screen and a table of error codes E1-E6 with causes and fixes.

sections.title: Firmware release notes v3 2
sections.text: Nimbus X2 Firmware 3.2.0 Release Notes Release date: 22 September 2026. Rollout: staged, 10% -> 50% -> 100% over two weeks.

sections.title: Highlights
sections.text: Adaptive Recovery learns your home's heating and cooling rates and pre-conditions before schedule changes. Monthly Energy Reports in the Nimbus app compare usage with the previous year. Boot time reduced from 9.4 s to 5.1 s. Fixes brown-out resets on some power-stealing installations (E2 errors).
sections.summary: Summarizes the headline changes in 3.2.0: Adaptive Recovery, monthly energy reports, faster boot and a power-stealing stability fix.

sections.title: Adaptive Recovery
sections.text: Adaptive Recovery observes how quickly the home heats and cools over the first 7 days after it is enabled. It then starts heating or cooling ahead of each schedule change so the target is reached on time. Early start is capped at 2 hours and is disabled in Eco mode. The feature is on by default for new installs and off by default for existing users, who will be prompted in the app.
sections.summary: Explains how Adaptive Recovery estimates heating/cooling rates over 7 days and caps early start at 2 hours.

sections.title: Energy Reports
sections.text: On the first day of each month, the app generates an energy report showing heating, cooling and Eco runtime, plus a comparison with the same month last year. Reports require at least 30 days of history. Figure 1: Energy report screen in the Nimbus mobile app
sections.summary: Describes the monthly energy report screen showing runtime by mode and comparison with last year.

sections.title: Bug Fixes
sections.text: ID Issue Affected versions FW-1822 Brown-out reset during Wi-Fi TX on power-stealing installs (E2) 3.0.0 - 3.1.4 FW-1850 Schedule shifted by one hour after daylight saving change 3.1.0 - 3.1.4 FW-1861 Humidity reading stuck at 0% after sensor soft reset 3.1.2 - 3.1.4 FW-1877 Fan kept running for 90 s after cooling ended despite 'Fan: Auto' 3.1.4 FW-1893 Display did not wake on approach when ambient light below 5 lux 3.0.0 - 3.1.4 FW-1902 BLE setup failed on some Android 16 devices 3.1.3 - 3.1.4
sections.summary: Lists six fixed issues with their ticket IDs, including E2 brown-outs and schedule drift across daylight saving changes.

sections.title: Known Issues
sections.text: On some early EVT units, the update log shows 'display calibration table missing'. This is harmless; default calibration is used. (FW-1910) Energy reports may take up to 24 hours to appear for dual-fuel heat pump systems. (FW-1915)
sections.summary: Lists open issues in 3.2.0 such as a missing display calibration table warning and slow reports for heat pump systems.

sections.title: Upgrade Procedure
sections.text: Most customers receive the update automatically overnight. Lab and field-test units can be updated manually with the nimbus-cli tool: 1. Connect your computer to the same network as the thermostat. 2. Run nimbus-cli device update --serial <serial> --fw 3.2.0. 3. Wait for the device to reboot (about 60 seconds). Do not remove the display during the update. 4. Confirm the version under Menu > Settings > About. Figure 2: Example nimbus-cli output for a successful update to 3.2.0
sections.summary: Gives the steps for updating via the app or via the nimbus-cli tool for lab units, with example command output.
